card.name: Prepositions after a defining noun
card.fires_on: Short prepositions such as in, of, for and on that follow a noun in a dictionary or encyclopedia style definition. They often come before words like all, the or a place or topic.

modes.label: In after body-material nouns
modes.description: The word in after a noun like material or cells, before all cells or the cortex.
modes.example: It helps maintain healthy nerve cells and red blood cells and is also needed to make DNA, the genetic material<< in>> all cells.

modes.label: For/on/of after a descriptive noun
modes.description: A preposition linking a defined thing to its scope or subject, as in resource on or center for.
modes.example: The Catholic Encyclopedia is the most comprehensive resource<< on>> Catholic teaching, history, and information ever

card.plain: It marks the small linking word in a definition, such as 'found in all cells' or 'resource on a topic'.
